messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: high 5xx rate for /v1/generate in eu-west1 (5xx_rate=8.7% over 2m; threshold=4.0%). Auto-pager sent to oncall rotation (PD-INC-9742). Links: https://pagerduty.example/PD-INC-9742, runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-5xx

jamie_oncall: acked via PagerDuty (PD-INC-9742). I'm oncall for the next 60m. Initial hypothesis: spike started ~1756543080 after a config push to dedicated pool autoscaler earlier. Anyone seen related deploys? :eyes:

maya: seeing the same in grafana. 5xx are mainly 502/504 from inference-gateway -> runtime p95 token processing time jumped. No new model rollouts in eu-west1, but autoscaler changed min replicas earlier (PR #4123). Pulling logs now.

raj: I rolled the autoscaler PR but only modified min/max; didn't touch routing. No canary. I can revert if needed but want to confirm cause.

lucas: Support has a few customers reporting errors: "AcmePay" and "Clipper" hitting failures on embeddings calls. CS told customers we're investigating. No broad outage yet but some drop in success rate.

maya: logs from gateway (snippet):
```
[2025-08-05T02:34:12Z] upstream: timeout after 10s while waiting kv-cache lookup
[2025-08-05T02:34:13Z] worker: failed to fetch kv-page: context deadline exceeded
[2025-08-05T02:34:14Z] runtime: request canceled, upstream 502
```
Looks like KV cache layer has elevated latencies leading to upstream timeouts -> 502. Correlates with autoscaler reducing warm replicas earlier.

jamie_oncall: good find. Action plan: 1) temporarily route traffic to fallback model variant in eu-west1 to reduce backend load, 2) scale up dedicated pool to warm instances, 3) reduce retry aggressiveness at gateway for 60m. I'll start 1 & 2.

maya: running health checks and scaling commands now. Command used:
```
# scale dedicated pool
redwoodctl pool scale --region eu-west1 --pool inference-dedicated-eu --replicas 12
# set routing policy to fallback
redwoodctl routing set --region eu-west1 --service inference --policy fallback-variant
```

pagerbot: Automation: scaling job started (job-id: scale-7862). Expected to finish in ~90s. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

raj: I can temporarily increase the KV cache size config on nodes, pushing config now. Will monitor.

kim: tagging oncall - if routing/fallthrough works we should see 5xx drop quickly. Prep a rollback of the autoscaler PR if this doesn't stabilize in 10m.

lucas: CS updated customers with a short note: "We're seeing elevated 5xx for generation endpoints in eu-west1 and are actively mitigating. ETA 30m." They asked for an incident severity label.

jamie_oncall: marking this as SEV-2 for now. PD ticket updated. Notifying account reps for AcmePay.

pagerbot: scale job completed successfully. Instances bootstrapped (12 -> ready). route update applied.

maya: after routing to fallback and scale up, metrics: 5xx rate down to 3.1% at 1756543600. p50 latency slightly up but overall success improved. Still seeing intermittent 502s from a small subset of pods.

jamie_oncall: I'm running a rolling restart on the gateway pods that show repeated upstream timeouts. Command:
```
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/inference-gateway -l region=eu-west1
```
Do we need to throttle incoming requests from known noisy clients? Could reduce tail risk.

raj: added a temporary client-level rate limit for top noisy keys (AcmePay bursts) at the gateway layer. Config push done: `gateway.cfg` updated + applied.

lucas: AcmePay reports errors are dropping. They said they saw ~30% failures earlier, now ~5%. They appreciate the quick response.

maya: gateway restarts complete; I see the remaining 502s trace back to one misbehaving node that failed to warm kv-cache. I've cordoned it and recreated the node. `kubectl drain node/node-7eu` then recreate.

jamie_oncall: node recreated. Monitoring.

pagerbot: Alert resolved (5xx_rate < threshold for 5m). Auto-ticket will be closed unless updated. :white_check_mark:

maya: marking incident as mitigated. Creating short incident doc with timeline and action items.

kim: thanks team. Post-incident actions: 1) revert autoscaler PR to previous safe defaults or add pre-warm step, 2) improve runbook to include immediate kv-cache checks, 3) add synthetic canary for KV latency, 4) add automatic client burst protection. Assign owners in ticket.

jamie_oncall: adding owners: raj -> autoscaler config, maya -> runbook + synthetic, lucas -> customer comms, kim -> postmortem. I'll stay onwatch for 30m then handoff to next oncall.

lucas: CS to follow up with AcmePay & Clipper with post-incident summary.

maya: log snippets and metrics graphs attached to the PD ticket (PD-INC-9742). Will write the postmortem draft.

jamie_oncall: handing off in 35m. If anything spikes, re-open PD. Thanks :thumbsup:

kim: good work. Closing our Slack thread once postmortem is linked.
